thesisQuality.note: $57.3B backlog, $6.7B Q2 awards and carrier long-lead funding demonstrate durable demand; execution/cash conversion prevent exceptional band.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Revenue +10.9% and operating margin +80 bps support strong operating trend, offset by sharply negative Q2 and first-half cash conversion.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: Current independent market evidence supplies price/earnings context but not rare asymmetry; conservative mixed/balanced band retained.

catalystScore.note: Raised shipbuilding guidance, carrier long-lead award and automation programs provide multiple source-supported medium-term catalysts.

governancePower.note: Management raised guidance while disclosing cash-conversion pressure; adequate transparency and execution evidence, but cost/schedule risks remain.

alignment2036.note: Nuclear-carrier and naval shipbuilding capacity plus autonomy/automation are foundational defense-industrial capabilities with long-duration demand.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Core shipbuilding plus mission/autonomy capabilities provide several demand channels, though U.S. government concentration remains high.

bottleneckControl.note: Specialized U.S. nuclear-carrier/shipyard capacity has long lead times and high qualification/switching barriers.

scenarioRobustness.note: Large backlog and multiple naval/mission programs support resilience, tempered by government concentration and execution sensitivity.

substitutionResilience.note: Nuclear-carrier and complex naval shipbuilding require specialized facilities, labor and qualification that are difficult to replace quickly.

supplyChainResilience.note: Long-lead material funding improves planning, but disclosed labor/supplier and schedule dependencies remain meaningful.

pricingPower.note: Operating margin improved despite execution pressures, supporting some economic capture, but government contracting and cash conversion constrain evidence of durable pricing power.

risk.note: Material labor/supplier, schedule, government-concentration and cash-conversion risks coexist with strong backlog and strategic demand.

confidence.note: Current SEC-filed financials plus issuer contract/capacity evidence and independent market context cover all score components; issuer concentration and unresolved cash-conversion tension prevent higher confidence.

thesis: HII controls scarce U.S. naval shipbuilding capacity with durable backlog and modernization catalysts; upside depends on converting demand and automation into throughput, margins and cash.
keyRisk: Execution and cash conversion can lag backlog and revenue because labor, suppliers, schedules and government program concentration constrain realization.
nextCatalyst: Evidence of shipbuilding throughput/margin and operating/free-cash conversion improvement against raised FY26 guidance.
